methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Hgen is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Colin Ho and Molly Yang that has raised $7M to date. The climate and energy sector includes a comparison universe of nine private firms and one public company (Lnza), though seed-stage peers within this universe are sparse. Relevant private comparables include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, though these span later stages and varying valuations.

Given the lack of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers in climate and energy with comparable scale, only the stage-progression method is applicable here. This approach uses the $7M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $18M. This method does not rely on peer medians, which cannot be reliably calculated from the available peer set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $20M, centered on $18M. Key uncertainties stem from the thinness of comparable datapoints at the seed stage within climate and energy; a peer-median cross-check would require additional comparable companies at similar stages and valuations. The reliance on a single method introduces model risk, and actual valuation should incorporate operational milestones, funding trajectory, and sector-specific capital intensity not reflected in this quantitative framework.
